reaction.episode: CORRECTION episode through the Nov 13 close: SPX is 3.61% below its 120-day high, 1.38% below its 50-day but 3.02% above its 200-day; SMH sits in Zone 2 at $486.75 (down 27.55% from its high, 13.05% below its 50-day) while NVDA is below Zone 2 at $162.85 (down 33.09%, RSI 24.9); VIX 19.30 and HY OAS 3.20 are both calm, and the mechanical capitulation tally is 2 of 4.
reaction.invalidation: A SPX close below its 200-day near 7,340 with HY OAS breaking above 4% voids Watch and flips the read from correction/rotation to a confirmed rollover; conversely a clean NVDA earnings beat with SMH reclaiming $505 and the tally at 3 of 4 voids the wait and arms Tranche A.

ladder.response: Escalation to the next zone down: Tranche A stays un-armed, no new probes, hold existing positions and bills; the next deployment zone becomes SMH $440-460 / NVDA $140-150 on a confirmed second low only
ladder.trigger: SMH closes below $470 (Zone 2 floor) or NVDA closes below $150

ladder.response: Trap case: do not chase the first bounce — treat a failed retest of the failure zone as confirmation of the correction, trim into strength on any position that recovered to its failure-zone level, and wait for the second-low verdict
ladder.trigger: SPX rallies toward the 7,750-7,820 failure zone or SMH toward $580-600 and fails

ladder.response: Stand-down: all deployment pauses per the ladder rules, existing exposure is held but no probes are sized, until VIX is back under 25 and HY OAS back under 4%
ladder.trigger: VIX closes above 25 or HY OAS breaks above 4%

ladder.response: Re-entry: Probe Tranche A sizing per the ladder — SMH $470-505 / NVDA $175-185 zone prints with the tally at 3 or better, sized as a probe not a full tranche until the second low holds
ladder.trigger: NVDA earnings Nov 17 resolves the catalyst AND SMH holds Zone 2 AND the mechanical tally reaches 3 of 4 (volume climax reversal or VIX rollover confirms)

reaction.trapRisk: The first bounce is the trap case: SMH is 13.05% below its 50-day and NVDA's RSI is 24.9, so a sharp relief rally into the SPX 7,750-7,820 / SMH $580-600 failure zone is likely to be sold. Do not chase the first bounce and do not size probes on it — entries only after the failure-zone retest verdict, or on a confirmed second low holding with the tally at 3 of 4.

strategyPosture: Watch. The tape is a correction with rotation, not a rollover — SPX is only 3.61% off its high and credit is calm — but the deployment tally is 2 of 4 and NVDA's catalyst is unresolved until its Nov 17 earnings, so no new money moves until the tally confirms or the catalyst clears.

themes.counterRead: The divergence is real and worth tracking, not dismissing: a 12.93-point Mag7/SPY gap with the index's heaviest weights unwinding can drag the index down if credit flips. The read holds only while HY OAS stays contained and lending stays loose — if either cracks, rotation becomes rollover.
themes.dataAnchor: The index itself is barely dented — SPX is only 3.61% below its 120-day high (7,561.67 close vs 7,844.52 high) and 3.02% above its 200-day. The weakness is concentrated: Mag7 names average 16.43% below their 52-week highs against SPY at 3.5%, a 12.93-point divergence gap, with NVDA the weakest at -33.1% and AAPL the strongest at -1.3%. Credit confirms the rotation read: lending standards are LOOSE (SLOOS 1.7%, far below the ~40% stress threshold) and HY OAS is 3.20, calm.
themes.label: Concentration rotation, not rollover
themes.narrative: The tape reads as a broad market break: QQQ fell 2.02% on Friday and is down 7.38% over the month, with the AI complex leading the decline.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS breaking above 4% or SLOOS tightening toward stress levels would reclassify this as a rollover.

themes.counterRead: Fundamentals ahead of price is the setup, but the catalyst is unresolved and real: NVDA reports Tuesday Nov 17 after the close, the first call under interim CEO Colette Kress. An oversold RSI plus an open scandal is not a buy signal — it is a setup that needs the earnings verdict before sizing. Do not probe into the print.
themes.dataAnchor: NVDA is $162.85, 33.1% below its 52-week high with RSI 24.9 (oversold), yet revenue is growing 61.4% year over year and the opportunity engine scores it 83 with a RECOVERY revenue inflection. SMH sits in Zone 2 at $486.75, down 27.55% from its high and 13.05% below its 50-day. The decline reason is tagged ACUTE_CATALYST, not a broken business — the catalyst is a governance/financing story, not a demand collapse.
themes.label: AI infrastructure unwind
themes.narrative: The market believes the AI trade is broken — NVDA fell 12.75% on the week, its sixth straight weekly decline, on the circular-finance scandal and leadership turmoil.
themes.watchFor: NVDA earnings Tue Nov 17 after the close: guidance on the neocloud loans and a reclaim of the $175 Zone 2 floor on a close.

themes.counterRead: Insider buying plus a confirmed earnings print against a 30-50% drawdown is the classic data-ahead pattern, but the theme rides the same AI-capex narrative as NVDA — if hyperscaler capex guidance disappoints at NVDA earnings, power names re-rate down with it regardless of their own prints. The dislocation is real; the timing trigger is not VST's own numbers, it is NVDA's.
themes.dataAnchor: VST is $133.01, 29.7% below its high, but insiders bought $1.17M at the trough, revenue is growing 19.1% year over year, and the opportunity engine scores it 83 with a durable-moat thesis at a cyclical trough. BWXT is 49.1% below its high with revenue growing 18.3% and positive free cash flow of $185M. The theme's own Q3 print confirmed to the upside (EPS $3.25 vs $2.98 consensus), so the selloff is sentiment, not a thesis break.
themes.label: Nuclear / AI power
themes.narrative: The power trade is being sold as collateral damage of the AI unwind — SMR fell 5.00% Friday and is down 25.55% over the month, OKLO down 22.56%, CCJ down 15.57%, VST down 15.00%.
themes.watchFor: VST holding above its $133 level through NVDA earnings, and any hyperscaler capex cut in NVDA's Nov 17 guidance.

themes.counterRead: Multiple compression is a legitimate repricing when rates sit at 5.10% on the 10-year — these are not mispriced by accident, they are repriced for a higher discount rate. The opportunity is real only if revenue growth holds through the next prints; DDOG and ONTO have no earnings before Jan 15, 2027, so the next hard check is a long way off and patience is the position.
themes.dataAnchor: The numbers run the other way: DDOG revenue is growing 27.7% year over year with 80% gross margin and $1,001M free cash flow (29.2% margin), scored 82, the top conviction name. ONTO revenue is up 41.5% while the stock sits 47.3% below its high, scored 81. AVGO revenue is up 55% with 67.8% gross margin and $26,914M free cash flow, scored 81. The decline reasons are SENTIMENT_DRIVEN and MULTIPLE_COMPRESSION across the board — no deteriorating-revenue signal in the top names.
themes.label: Enterprise software dislocation
themes.narrative: Software is being priced as if enterprise AI spending has stalled — NOW is down 41.6% from its high with RSI 31.9, DDOG down 38.8%, SNOW down 24.3%.
themes.watchFor: Any of DDOG, ONTO, or AVGO breaking to new 52-week lows on no news would signal the compression is becoming a growth problem, not a rate problem.

themes.counterRead: A 10-year above 5% is doing real work against equity multiples — it is the reason software and AI names are compressing rather than collapsing. The risk is a move above 5.2% sustained, which would flip the regime read and put the Tranche-2 trigger zone in play. Until then, rates are a headwind, not a break.
themes.dataAnchor: The 10-year is 5.10% — below the 5.2% falsifier line, with the 2s10s curve at +0.24 (steepening, not inverting) and the real 10-year at 2.86%. The Fed funds rate is 3.88% against a 2-year at 4.86%. Credit is calm: HY OAS 3.20, not cracking, and VIX is 19.30, up 3.21% on the day but with no spike rollover (5-day high 19.92). The bond market is pricing higher-for-longer, not distress.
themes.label: Rates and credit regime
themes.narrative: The news flow is split: December rate-hike talk is rising while rate-cut hopes fade, and the FOMC minutes land Wed Nov 18 with the Dec 8-9 decision behind them.
themes.watchFor: 10-year closing above 5.2% sustained, or FOMC minutes Nov 18 confirming a December hike.
